name: Lachung village homestays
price_band: ₹1,500–2,500 per room per night with meals
summary: Family-run rooms in the older part of Lachung, across the river from the main road. Simple, warm hospitality and home-cooked meals at the lowest price in the valley.
body: Several Lachung families let two to four rooms in their wooden or concrete homes, mostly on the quieter side of the river. Rooms have thick quilts, basic furniture and either an attached bathroom or one shared with another room. Hot water comes from a geyser or a bucket, and power cuts are common.

Meals are eaten with the family or in a small dining room: rice, dal, vegetables, eggs or chicken, and thukpa or momo on request. Your operator can book a homestay instead of a hotel on any Lachung package, often at a small saving. Ask about heaters in winter.
why: Cheapest decent beds in Lachung, usually with all meals
Money goes straight to village families
Quieter than the hotel strip on the highway
Hosts can explain the Dzumsa, the monastery and village life

faqs.q: Can I book a Lachung homestay without a tour operator?
faqs.a: You can contact a homestay directly, but you still need a registered operator for the permit and vehicle. Most people ask their operator to book the homestay as part of the package. Tell them early, as homestays have few rooms.

faqs.q: Are Lachung homestays warm enough in winter?
faqs.a: Rooms are cold from November to March. Thick quilts are standard, and some homes have electric blankets or a heater for an extra charge. Bring thermals and confirm what heating is available before you book. A hot water bottle and woollen socks make nights much easier.

Yes. Simple vegetarian meals of rice, dal and seasonal vegetables are always possible. Jain or vegan food needs advance notice. Meat dishes such as chicken or pork are cooked on request. Tell your operator about diet needs when booking so the host can buy supplies, as shops in Lachung are small.

name: Le Coxy Resort
price_band: ₹4,000–7,000 per room per night with meals
summary: An established mid-range resort in Lachung with wooden-finished rooms and valley views, commonly used on Value packages. Reliable service and meals at a fair price for the valley.
body: Le Coxy Resort is one of the better-known mid-range properties in Lachung, with rooms in a few categories, a dining hall serving Indian, Chinese and local food, and views across the valley. Rooms are clean and warmer than average, with geysers and heaters available.

It suits travellers who want more comfort than a homestay without paying top rates. Packages normally include dinner and breakfast. Prices rise sharply in April, May and October, so book early in those months.
why: Good balance of comfort and price in Lachung
Hot water and room heaters available
Reliable meals for early Yumthang starts
Used regularly by Gangtok operators, so easy to book on a package

faqs.q: Does Le Coxy Resort have heating?
faqs.a: Room heaters are usually available, sometimes for an extra charge in winter. Confirm when booking, especially from November to March when nights go below freezing in Lachung. Hot water comes from geysers, which can be affected by power cuts. Carry thermals in any case, as corridors and dining areas are cold.

faqs.q: Is breakfast early enough for Yumthang?
faqs.a: The kitchen is used to dawn departures and can serve an early breakfast or pack one. Tell reception the night before what time your driver is leaving. If you leave very early, ask for tea and a packed breakfast, and eat at the stalls in Yumthang if you are hungry.

Most guests book through a Gangtok tour operator as part of a permit package, which often gets a better rate. Direct bookings are possible, but you still need the operator for permit and vehicle. Ask your operator to confirm the room category in writing, and book early for April, May and October.

name: Yarlam Resort
price_band: ₹7,000–12,000 per room per night with meals
summary: One of the most comfortable resorts in Lachung, with larger rooms, better heating and mountain views. Our Comfort-tier choice for the Lachung valley.
body: Yarlam Resort sits on the slopes of Lachung and is among the better-appointed places in North Sikkim, with spacious wood-finished rooms, attached baths with reliable hot water, room heating and a restaurant serving a wide menu.

It is a good choice for honeymooners, older travellers and anyone who sleeps badly in cold rooms. Like everywhere in North Sikkim, it is still a mountain property: expect occasional power cuts and a simpler setup than a city hotel.
why: Among the warmest and most comfortable rooms in Lachung
Good food and attentive service for the area
Views over the valley
Calmer than the hotels on the main road

faqs.q: Is Yarlam Resort worth the higher price?
faqs.a: If warmth and comfort matter to you, yes. Lachung nights are cold, and better heating and hot water make a real difference after a dawn trip to Zero Point. Budget travellers will be fine in a homestay. Prices rise in peak months, so compare rates early.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of the better options for couples in Lachung, with larger rooms and views. Ask for a valley-facing room and check whether any special arrangements cost extra. Book well ahead for April, May, October and December, when the best rooms fill first.

faqs.q: Do I still need a tour operator?
faqs.a: Yes. Permits and registered vehicles for Lachung come through registered operators. Ask your operator to add Yarlam as the hotel on your package. Private cars from outside cannot go beyond the checkposts. Book the resort through the operator, or tell them if you have booked it yourself.

name: Lachen village lodges and homestays
price_band: ₹1,500–3,000 per room per night with meals
summary: Simple family-run lodges and homestays in Lachen, used by almost every Gurudongmar package. Basic, warm-hearted and set up for 4 am starts.
body: Lachen has fewer and simpler places to stay than Lachung. Most are small lodges or homestays with plain rooms, thick quilts, attached or shared bathrooms and a dining room serving dinner and an early breakfast or packed meal.

Facilities are basic: power cuts and lukewarm water are common, and heating is rare. But staff understand the Gurudongmar routine and will wake you, feed you and have you in the car on time. A few better hotels exist at higher prices if you ask your operator.
why: The only way to reach Gurudongmar is to sleep in Lachen
Hosts know the dawn routine well
Low prices with meals included
Quiet village setting

faqs.q: Are there better hotels in Lachen?
faqs.a: A handful of better-built hotels charge about ₹3,500–7,000 a room with meals. Standards are still simpler than Lachung. Ask your operator for the best available if comfort matters, and book early in peak months. Even the better places may have power cuts and limited heating.

faqs.q: Will I get hot water in Lachen?
faqs.a: Usually, by geyser or bucket, though power cuts can interrupt it. Many travellers skip a bath before the 4 am Gurudongmar start and wash on return. Carry wet wipes. In winter, ask for a bucket of hot water at a set time rather than relying on the geyser.

faqs.q: Can I stay two nights in Lachen?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is a good idea for acclimatisation. Tell your operator when booking, as most packages assume one night. Expect to pay for an extra night of room and vehicle. The extra night is also a chance to visit the monastery and walk the village.

name: Lepcha homestays in Dzongu
price_band: ₹1,500–2,500 per person per night with all meals
summary: Family homestays in Lepcha villages such as Lingthem, Passingdang and Hee Gyathang. The main way to stay in the reserve, and one of the most rewarding stays in Sikkim.
body: Dzongu has no hotels. Instead, a number of Lepcha families run homestays with a few clean, simple rooms, many with attached bathrooms. Meals are home-cooked from the family farm, and hosts arrange guides, walks and the Dzongu permit.
Rates usually include all meals. Prices are per person rather than per room. Book a few weeks ahead and send ID copies early so the host can arrange your entry papers.
why: The only way to stay inside the Lepcha reserve
Hosts arrange the Dzongu permit and local guides
Home-cooked Lepcha food
Low altitude and quiet, a good pause between high valleys

faqs.q: How do I book a Dzongu homestay?
faqs.a: Contact a homestay by phone or message, or ask a Gangtok operator who works with Dzongu hosts. Share ID copies so the host can arrange the permit. Confirm pickup from Mangan and the total price including meals. Book a few weeks ahead for October to December.

They are simple but clean, with good bedding and usually attached bathrooms. Do not expect hotel features. Some have geysers, others bucket hot water. Power cuts happen, so carry a torch. Most hosts keep rooms very clean and serve generous meals.

faqs.q: Is the price per room or per person?
faqs.a: Most Dzongu homestays quote per person per night, including all meals. Children usually pay less. Guides and vehicles are extra. Ask for the full price in writing before you travel. Prices may also rise slightly in the October to December peak.
